stories.description: Low oxygen levels in the brain, or cerebral anoxia, are a leading cause of death worldwide. Patients who recover from cerebral anoxia deal with persistent neurological issues that worsen their quality of life. Building on previous work showing that brain–heart interactions can predict the severity of symptoms and survival, Diego Candia-Rivera, Sofia Carrion-Falgarona and colleagues from the Paris Brain Institute assessed whether brain–heart interactions in a rat model of severe oxygen loss can predict survival after resuscitation. The work is published in eNeuro.

stories.title: Agreement among large language models does not track medical truth in health claim verification
stories.description: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as tools to verify online health information. A common assumption from the self-consistency and ensemble literature is that agreement across models signals reliability. But it remains untested whether inter-model consensus tracks medical truth. We evaluated 10 LLMs spanning frontier, Russian-specific and medical-specialized families on RuHealth, a corpus of 108 short health claims (40 true, 40 false, 28 disputed) validated through multi-stage physician review. Each claim was classified as true, false, or disputed, in both Russian and a validated English translation, across decoding temperatures and 3 stochastic runs ($${\sim }$$90,000 judgements). Frontier models were most accurate (macro-F1 64–70) but no model was reliable: “disputed” was assigned to 59.8% of judgements versus a 26% true base rate, while false claims were systematically missed. Majority voting did not help. Three frontier models were unanimous on 90 of 108 claims, yet 31% of those unanimous verdicts were wrong, and 26 of 28 assigned “disputed” to claims that were actually true (14) or false (12). Thus, in this setting on health claims, agreement among contemporary LLMs is not evidence of medical correctness; this effect, which we term consensus mirage, proves to be robust to prompt wording and language.
